newsitem.title: USA: Outline of major UAW-Ford contract points.
newsitem.headline: Outline of major UAW-Ford contract points.

text.p: Here is a summary of the major items contained in the tentative labour contract reached Monday between the United Auto Workers and Ford Motor Co. The information comes from a report handed out to members of the UAW National Ford Council on Wednesday.
--TOTAL ECONOMIC GAINS: $13,910 for typical UAW worker over life of three year contract;
--TERMS: $2,000 lump sum payment in first year, followed by 3 percent base wage increases in second and third year;
--WAGES: base wage for assembly worker will be $21.60 at end of new contract, versus $17.945 at end of previous pact;
--PENSIONS: 13 percent increase in monthly payment to $2,295 for workers with at least 30 years of service who retire during the contract before age 62;
--JOB GUARANTEES: Employment at UAW-Ford plants will stay at or above 95 percent of current levels, unless the company experiences severe, market-driven layoffs;
--COST OF LIVING: unchanged formula for computing cost-of-living allowances;
--TUITION ASSISTANCE: up to $1,000 annual payment for each child up to 25 years old of an active, retired or deceased worker;
--TIERED WAGES: no change in starting wages for new hires, who start at 70 percent of full wage and take three years to reach parity;
--NEW PARTS WORKERS: Ford can pay lower wages and benefits to workers in new component business that do not compete with existing UAW Ford workers in same industry segment or geographic area;
--OUTSOURCING: Ford faces no broad restrictions on farming out work to suppliers, but UAW will become involved in sourcing desions at earlier stage.
--HEALTH CARE: Workers retain fully paid health care benefits and receive several improvements in coverage;
--OTHER BENEFITS: annual Christmas bonus of up to $600; 48 paid holidays during life of contract, including newly negotiated holiday on Veterans Day, Nov. 13, 1998.
